bel0: Yes. BMI shows excess weight but not where the fat is stored. Waist-to-height ratio is a practical estimate of fat around the middle. In a 2012 meta-analysis pooling studies, waist-to-height ratio was a better screening tool for heart and metabolic risk factors in adults than waist circumference or BMI. People from some ethnic backgrounds are more prone to storing fat around the middle, and their risk of weight-related conditions rises at a lower BMI.
